title: Determination of Local Diagnostic Reference Values for Paediatric Radiography
summary:
When it comes to X-ray examinations of children, the guiding principle is: as high a image quality as necessary, as little radiation as possible. As children are considerably more sensitive to radiation than adults, radiation protection is particularly important in this context. However, there are currently no official comparative values (known as diagnostic reference levels) for many X-ray examinations in children, which hospitals can use as a guide to avoid unnecessarily high radiation exposure.
This study aims to bridge this gap. To this end, X-ray data from day-to-day clinical practice at various hospitals is being collected and analysed. The aim is to establish reliable reference values for radiation dose for as many types of examination for different age groups of children as possible.

interventions.name: Retrospective analysis of all patients in the age groups 0–1 year, 1–5 years, 5–10 years, 10–15 years, and 15–18 years who underwent a radiographic examination between 2020 and 2025.

criteria:
Inclusion criteria:
Data analysis of patients who underwent radiographic examinations between 2020 and 2025.
Exclusion criteria:
Examinations with missing or inadequate study descriptions or protocol information, which cannot be assigned to a specific type of examination.
Examinations with a dose area product of 0 cGy·cm².
